summary: Across both the 2014 and 2023 mayoral campaigns, Olivia Chow's Instagram content positions housing affordability as a top civic priority (t3QSr1utLV, CtIQZymtA3s). Chow frames Toronto as facing an affordability crisis driven by a decade of insufficient construction and inaction (Cr_i5mPJMRP, CsSOxZbAavJ, CspF_1zANJZ). Core commitments in 2023 include a City Homes Plan to build 25,000 rent-controlled homes over 8 years on city-owned land with the City acting as a public developer (Cr_Yy69ga2k, CseTHadgMsU), $100M per year to prevent renovictions (CtPRf7mgQPR, CtHTQmxAsFH), 1,000 to 3,000 new rent supplements (CsHejOWP0rO), a Renters Action Committee (CtkGd5mPLWL), and support for community land trusts (CtPRf7mgQPR). Chow also supports stronger tenant protections, building standards, and eviction prevention (CrwuyFLop4-, uY0e37utHo), and links housing to homelessness and food security (CrojPrcvfK2, CrZJPRIvr1f).

key_positions.stance: Toronto faces an affordability crisis rooted in a decade of insufficient housing construction and inaction
Supports the City acting as a public developer rather than relying on private developers alone
Supports building large quantities of new affordable, rent-controlled housing
Supports stronger renter protections, including against renovictions, demovictions, and above-guideline rent increases
Supports community ownership models such as community land trusts and co-op housing
Frames housing as linked to homelessness, food security, and gender-based violence supports
Supports culturally responsive housing for seniors and diverse communities

key_actions.action: Announced an affordable housing plan during the 2014 mayoral campaign
Announced the City Homes Plan to build 25,000 rent-controlled homes over 8 years on city-owned land
Released a renter protection plan funding measures to protect tenants
Pledged $100M per year to prevent renovictions and secure affordable homes, plus 3,000 rent supplements
Pledged to establish a Toronto Renters Action Committee
Met with renters, community land trust members, seniors, and United Way partners to discuss housing models
Pledged to fight federal cuts to co-op housing support affecting 29 co-ops
